topic_and_scope: Analysis of advanced implant surface engineering strategies (PEO/MAO, nanostructuring, hydroxyapatite and Ca-P coatings, and antibacterial modifications) to enhance osseointegration and minimize peri-implant infections in dental implants, with emphasis on translational challenges and long-term outcomes.
main_themes: Surface engineering for bone–implant integration and antimicrobial resistance
Nanostructured surfaces and ion-doped coatings: mechanisms and trade-offs
Clinical translation, standardization, and long-term outcomes
main_findings: Moderate surface roughness (1–2 μm) generally improves osseointegration, but excessive cervical roughness (>2 μm) is linked to higher peri-implantitis risk; nanoscale features can further enhance cellular responses but require coordinated microroughness.

Hydroxyapatite and other calcium-phosphate coatings can promote osseointegration in preclinical models, but clinical evidence for improved implant survival is inconsistent and concerns about coating delamination persist; nanoscale and incorporated antimicrobials show promise but require long-term validation.

key_gaps.description: Lack of standardized experimental procedures and measurement techniques across studies of implant surface modifications, hindering cross-study comparability.
Insufficient long-term, multi-site in vivo data on nanoscale surface modifications and PEO-based antibacterial/bioconductive coatings to establish safety, durability, and infection control benefits.

future_directions.title: Establish consensus guidelines for implant surface evaluation standards
future_directions.rationale: To address conflicting results across studies, convene a consortium of researchers, manufacturers, and clinicians to define standardized surface roughness ranges, coating criteria, and measurement protocols (profilometry, AFM, XRD, SEM). Propose a registry of methods and reporting standards, including in vitro assays and in vivo endpoints. Implement multi-center validation studies using common benchmarks to enable cross-study comparability and accelerate regulatory acceptance.

future_directions.title: Conduct long-term in vivo validation of Ca-P/HA PEO coatings on dental implants
future_directions.rationale: The literature shows improved osseointegration in preclinical studies but inconsistent clinical survival data and potential coating delamination. Design multi-year animal studies with standardized infection challenge models and include translational endpoints such as removal torque, histomorphometry, micro-CT, and infection biomarkers. If preclinical results are favorable, proceed to phased clinical trials in diverse patient populations with rigorous adverse event monitoring.

future_directions.title: Optimize PEO electrolyte formulations for HA incorporation with minimal delamination and cytotoxic risk
future_directions.rationale: Zn doping and Ca/P ratios can enhance bioactivity but high Zn may be cytotoxic; systematic exploration of DC vs AC regimes, electrolyte pH, and additive composition is needed. Use design-of-experiments to map coating thickness, porosity, phase composition, and mechanical adhesion. Validate with in vitro osteoblast/osteoclast assays and in vivo corrosion/biocompatibility tests, followed by short-term in vivo biocompatibility studies.

future_directions.title: Characterize immune responses to nanoscale and hierarchical surface topographies
future_directions.rationale: Understanding macrophage polarization and cytokine milieu in response to 70–100 nm nanotubes and microroughness is critical to balance osseointegration and infection resistance. Use in vitro co-cultures of macrophages with osteoblasts and epithelial cells, and in vivo models with immunohistochemistry and transcriptomics. Link immune profiles to bone formation and biofilm resistance outcomes to inform topography-driven design.

future_directions.title: Develop and test dual-function antibacterial-osteoconductive coatings
future_directions.rationale: There is a trade-off between antimicrobial activity and osteoblast compatibility; explore coatings that couple HA or Ca-P matrices with safe antimicrobial agents and/or surface topographies (LIPSS/nanotubes) that deter biofilm formation. Assess bacterial adhesion/biofilm formation, osteogenic differentiation, and in vivo infection outcomes in dental implant models. Prioritize formulations with low cytotoxicity and durable bone–implant bonding.

future_directions.title: Scale-up and clinical translation of TiO2 nanotube and Zr-containing coatings
future_directions.rationale: Laboratory-scale data suggest enhanced osseointegration and antibacterial potential, but manufacturing reproducibility, coating adhesion, and fatigue behavior under masticatory loads remain uncertain. Develop scalable manufacturing protocols compatible with existing production lines, perform fatigue and wear testing under simulated oral conditions, and run pilot clinical studies focusing on dental implants in load-bearing scenarios.

future_directions.title: Define design guidelines for microroughness and nanoroughness synergy
future_directions.rationale: Conflicting data on roughness parameters necessitate systematic synthesis of existing studies to derive practical design rules. Use meta-analysis and standardized testing to determine optimal roughness windows and microroughness–nanoroughness combinations that maximize osseointegration while minimizing infection risk. Translate findings into provable design guidelines for manufacturers.

future_directions.title: Integrate additive manufacturing with PEO coatings for porous implants
future_directions.rationale: 3D-printed porous titanium frameworks reduce stiffness mismatch and support vascularization but pose coating adhesion and homogenization challenges. Investigate how porosity and lattice architecture affect PEO coating thickness, adhesion strength, and long-term stability under cyclic loading. Validate in vivo for osseointegration and mechanical reliability in dental/orthopedic models, and develop industrial production guidelines.
